corrections.claim: 3(b) is not a measured-height rounding in the Kotlin strip walk but an explicit-height box clamping overflowing content; the paint band is the half-open [-w, 0), w = 3 and 5
corrections.measurement: PNG (orange rgb(255,165,0), tol 40), wave49-final CSS2/floats-clear: multicol-003 — ref y161-163 x235-334 n=300; web y161-163 identical; iOS y161-163 identical; ANDROID y158-160 x235-334 n=300 (shift -3, band 3 px). balancing-003 — ref/web/iOS y171-175 x235-334 n=500; ANDROID y166-170 n=500 (shift -5, band 5 px). Controls: multicol-002 and balancing-002 are ref-exact on Android. SOURCE confirms the mechanism split — 003/balancing-003 put the border on a NESTED `.bar` inside `.clear{clear:left;height:0}` (`border-bottom: orange solid` = medium 3px, and `5px orange solid`), while 002/balancing-002 put `border-bottom: solid orange` on the cleared box ITSELF and declare no height:0. Shift == band width in both movers ⇒ band-width dependent ⇒ not a strip-walk offset error.
corrections.correctedText: 3(b) Compose renders the 003/balancing-003 orange band w px too high, where w is the band's own width (003: Android y158-160 vs ref y161-163, w=3; balancing-003: Android y166-170 vs ref y171-175, w=5; both x235-334, both 300/500 px — measured on the wave49-final Android captures against the frozen refs). It is NOT a measured-height rounding in the Kotlin strip walk: a strip error would be band-width independent and would move columns 1-2, which are ref-exact, and the two siblings that put the border on the cleared box ITSELF (002 / balancing-002, no nested child, no height:0) are ref-exact on Android. The mechanism is an explicit `height:0` box handing its child FIXED 0 constraints (SizingApplier's LengthValue.Exact arm) so the nested `.bar` measures 0 tall, after which BorderSideApplier's `Side.BOTTOM -> Offset(0f, size.height - inset)` centres the stroke on -w/2, i.e. the half-open band [-w, 0). iOS is exact because .frame(height:) positions without shrinking the child. corrections.claim: 0(b)'s blocker was the channel LEVEL, not a declining resolver
corrections.verdict: CONFIRMED — both the queue entry and the corpus-v6.15 note are wrong as written
corrections.measurement: SOURCE — `PercentInsetResolve.resolve` returns `config` UNTOUCHED only at `if (cb.widthPx == null && cb.heightPx == null) return config`; with a width and a null height it resolves the block axis to 0.dp (`if (base == null) return 0.dp`). `PercentInsetPositioned.percentInsetPositioned` is a `Modifier.composed { }` factory, which materialises inside ComponentRenderer.RenderComponentContent — already INSIDE `LocalContainingBlock provides childContainingBlock` (ComponentRenderer.kt:1983). ARITHMETIC — position-relative-006's green div declares `width:100px; height:100px`, so the block IT publishes for its children is (100, 100) and `top: -10000%` resolves to 100 x -10000 / 100 = -10000 px; its own containing block is the parent `width:100px; min-height:100px` = (100, null), where the same code yields 0 px. So the resolver never declined on -006 — it resolved against the wrong level. PNG — Android paints 10000 px of (255,0,0) and ZERO green; web, iOS and the ref each paint 10000 px of (0,128,0). Cells: web P 0.9990 · iOS P 0.9974 · Android f 0.9966. NAMED WEAKNESS (B2 states it too): -10000% x 100 px == the legacy number-as-pixels -10000 px, so the capture alone cannot discriminate 'resolved at the wrong level' from 'declined and fell back'; the attribution rests on the code read plus that arithmetic identity, not on the pixel.
corrections.correctedText: 0(b) Compose percentage insets resolve against the WRONG containing block LEVEL. `PercentInsetPositioned` reads `LocalContainingBlock` from inside a `Modifier.composed { }` factory, which materialises inside `ComponentRenderer.RenderComponentContent` — already inside the component's own `LocalContainingBlock provides childContainingBlock` — so it reads the block the element publishes for its CHILDREN. On `css-position/position-relative-006` that is the green div's own (100, 100), and `top: -10000%` resolves to -10000 px; the element's real containing block is the parent's (100, null), where the same code correctly yields 0 px (CSS-indefinite ⇒ zero, css-position-3 relpos-insets). The Android capture paints 10000 px of pure red with zero green where web, iOS and the ref all paint 10000 px of (0,128,0). The wave-49 diagnosis in BOTH this entry and corpus-v6-15.json's _note — '`PercentInsetResolve` declines by design ... the prediction was optimistic; the code is right' — is WRONG: the resolver does not decline on -006 (neither cb axis is null at the level it is handed) and the code has a level bug. Landed: `layout/position/ElementContainingBlock.kt` + the read in `PercentInsetPositioned.kt`; the renderer `provides` line is applied at ComponentRenderer.kt:2001. Note that the -006 pixel cannot by itself distinguish the two hypotheses (-10000% x 100 px equals the legacy number-as-pixels value); the gate should confirm the predicted f -> P. corrections.claim: the new Compose line-box census is a twin of the wave-46 iOS LineClampCensus with exactly ONE stated divergence
corrections.verdict: REFUTED — there is a SECOND, unstated divergence
corrections.measurement:
LineBoxCensus.kt's banner says 'Twin of the wave-46 iOS StyleEngine/scrolling/LineClampCensus.swift ... same model, different file home' and names exactly one deliberate divergence (Compose maps Unprovable back onto the wave-41 uniform cap where Swift's `.unbounded` removes the cap). But `LineBoxCensusRuns.childRun` (Compose) carries an arm the Swift twin does not have at all: `if (tag == "br" || child.role == "line-break") return LineBoxRun(root.lineBoxPx, exactLines = 0, leadingBandPx = 0f)`. `LineClampCensusRuns.childRun` (iOS, lines 90-123) tests only `isDisplayNone`, then typography, then `explicitHeightPx`, then `isScrollContainer` — no tag and no role check — so a `
` whose measured `height` the converter stamps (the Compose comment records 0 or 20 px in this corpus) falls to the explicit-height leg and is budgeted as a MONOLITHIC box on iOS while contributing nothing on Compose. Behavioural impact on the corpus is UNMEASURED (no device this wave).
corrections.correctedText:
The Compose `LineBoxCensus` twin banner must name TWO divergences from the wave-46 iOS `LineClampCensus`, not one: (1) the stated Unprovable -> uniform-cap fallback vs Swift's `.unbounded`; and (2) Compose's `
` / `role == "line-break"` arm in `LineBoxCensusRuns.childRun`, which returns a zero-line zero-height run — the iOS `LineClampCensusRuns.childRun` has no tag or role check at all, so a `
` with the converter's stamped height is budgeted there as a monolithic box. Either port the arm to Swift or state the divergence in both headers; and measure it, because no corpus cell has been checked either way.
